title: the DSG nonweapon proficiencies chapter - the check system and Table 10, the slot economy, the artisans and NPC training, the optional bonuses, the craftsman and adventuring lists with Tables 11-13, and the XP option

banner.title: The DSG NONWEAPON PROFICIENCIES, R506: the printed pp. 23-29 (pdf 24-30) - the Proficiency Check system (the Ability Check frame with the listed die-roll modifiers, the improving +2 per additional slot, the quality ladder from success to the natural-20 flawless creation and the 110-200 percent pricing), the slot economy (the weapon-slot-buys-nonweapon one-way trade, the filled-slot immutability, the Secondary Skills conversion), the artisan ladder for NPCs, the optional DM bonuses, the fourteen craftsman descriptions, the fifteen adventuring descriptions and the XP-for-proficiencies option, with Table 10 (the 14 class rows), Table 11 (the 14 craftsman rows), Table 12 (the 11 weapon-making rows) and Table 13 (the 15 adventuring rows).
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the grids read from the IA djvu OCR at 300dpi coordinates with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read; the Weaver and Weaponsmith cells and the trainer/armorer slot cells carry the grids-file image cautions and are pinned as printed (the R501 precedent); the cross-book seam verified const-for-const against rules/wsgprof.h (R425) and rules/wsgprofd.h (R498) - NOTHING auto-credited; Table 10 agrees cell-for-cell with the WSG Table 1 pins, the shared Table 13 rows are SUBSTANTIALLY rebalanced (10 of 11 diverge), the shared description numbers agree whole.
banner.sentinel: The DSG Table 10/11/13 sign convention is the die-roll convention (negative easier), matching the WSG tables; the p. 23 prose example (+3 makes 12 equal 15) is the ability-score framing of the same modifiers. NA cells: ability 0, modifier 99, the bard as-other-classes row -1, the arrowhead per-day row -1.

consts.name: dnpCheckDieSides
consts.comment: the player rolls 1d20 and compares the result to the ability score.

consts.name: dnpCheckModifierExampleMod
consts.comment: a die-roll modifier example: a +3 modifier.

consts.name: dnpCheckModifierExampleRoll
consts.comment: a d20 roll of 12 with the +3 modifier.

consts.name: dnpCheckModifierExampleEq
consts.comment: the 12 roll with +3 is equal to a 15 for success.

consts.name: dnpImprovedStepPlus
consts.comment: improving a proficiency with an additional slot increases its modifier by 2.

consts.name: dnpImprovedExampleFrom
consts.comment: the improving example: a miner proficiency modifier of -1.

consts.name: dnpImprovedExampleTo
consts.comment: one additional slot raises the -1 miner modifier to +1.

consts.name: dnpProductPriceLoPct
consts.comment: quality products sell from 110 percent of the normal price.

consts.name: dnpProductPriceHiPct
consts.comment: quality products sell up to 200 percent of the normal price.

consts.name: dnpSecondarySkillsPerSlotLo
consts.comment: converting Secondary Skills takes one slot per one or two skills (low).

consts.name: dnpSecondarySkillsPerSlotHi
consts.comment: converting Secondary Skills takes one slot per one or two skills (high).

consts.name: dnpNpcNoWeaponYieldsNonweapon
consts.comment: an NPC who claims no weapon proficiency gets two nonweapon slots after apprenticeship training.

consts.name: dnpJourneymanYearsLo
consts.comment: after one year of journeyman practice (low).

consts.name: dnpJourneymanYearsHi
consts.comment: after up to four years of journeyman practice the character advances to master.

consts.name: dnpMasterArrivalSlot
consts.comment: the new master is granted one additional proficiency slot.

consts.name: dnpMasterYearsPerSlot
consts.comment: every four years of work thereafter gains one additional slot.

consts.name: dnpOptionalArmorPlusLo
consts.comment: improved nonmagical armor from strong metal: +1 (low).

consts.name: dnpOptionalArmorPlusHi
consts.comment: improved nonmagical armor from strong metal: +2 (high).

consts.name: dnpTrainerRoleMonths
consts.comment: training an animal for a typical role requires three months.

consts.name: dnpTrainerMaxAnimals
consts.comment: an animal trainer can have up to six animals in training at a given time.

consts.name: dnpTrainerEndMod
consts.comment: typical training grants a +10 modifier to the trainer check at the end of the period.

consts.name: dnpTrainerAdvancedMonths
consts.comment: additional training to add functions requires another three months.

consts.name: dnpTrainerAdvancedMax
consts.comment: no more than three animals during additional training.

consts.name: dnpArmorWeeksPerACPoint
consts.comment: armor takes two weeks of work per level of AC below 10.

consts.name: dnpArmorShieldWeeks
consts.comment: a shield (one AC point below 10) requires two weeks.

consts.name: dnpArmorFullPlateWeeks
consts.comment: a suit of full plate (nine AC points below 10) requires 18 weeks.

consts.name: dnpArmorFlawedWithin
consts.comment: a failed check within four of the needed amount creates usable but flawed armor.

consts.name: dnpArmorFlawedACWorse
consts.comment: flawed armor functions as one Armor Class worse than usual.

consts.name: dnpArmorBreaksOnLo
consts.comment: flawed armor struck in melee breaks on a natural 19.

consts.name: dnpArmorBreaksOnHi
consts.comment: flawed armor struck in melee breaks on a natural 20.

consts.name: dnpArmorBreakACDrop
consts.comment: broken armor drops the AC immediately by four classes.

consts.name: dnpArmorBreakACCap
consts.comment: the broken-armor AC drop never takes the AC above 10.

consts.name: dnpArmorRemoveRoundsDie
consts.comment: removing broken armor requires 1d4 rounds.

consts.name: dnpArmorBrokenMoveNum
consts.comment: in broken armor the character moves at 1/2 rate (numerator).

consts.name: dnpArmorBrokenMoveDen
consts.comment: in broken armor the character moves at 1/2 rate (denominator).

consts.name: dnpArmorBrokenAttackMod
consts.comment: in broken armor the character suffers -4 on all attack rolls.

consts.name: dnpBoatMaxLenFt
consts.comment: the boatwright can build watercraft up to 60 feet long.

consts.name: dnpBoatWeeksPerFoot
consts.comment: a boat requires one week of construction time per foot of length.

consts.name: dnpBoatCrewPerFtDen
consts.comment: a maximum of one boatwright per five-foot length can work simultaneously.

consts.name: dnpBoatFeatureWeeks
consts.comment: a cabin or sealed hold adds about a week apiece.

consts.name: dnpBoatUnskilledPerSkilled
consts.comment: two unskilled helpers equal the time savings of one additional skilled boatwright.

consts.name: dnpBowWeeks
consts.comment: a long or short bow takes one week of construction.

consts.name: dnpCompositeBowWeeks
consts.comment: a composite bow takes two weeks.

consts.name: dnpArrowsPerDayDie
consts.comment: 1d6 arrows can be made in one day.

consts.name: dnpFineBowRangeBonusIn
consts.comment: a natural 20 on the bow check increases the range by +2 inches for all range classes.

consts.name: dnpBowBreaksOnAttack
consts.comment: a failed bow breaks when the character using it rolls an unmodified 1 on a d20 attack.

consts.name: dnpBowFineDamageBonus
consts.comment: the fine-quality bow inflicts +1 damage on all successful attacks.

consts.name: dnpBowFineNat20AttackBonus
consts.comment: a natural 20 on the fine-quality check adds +1 to all attack rolls.

consts.name: dnpCarpenterCubeFt
consts.comment: a single carpenter builds a wooden object the size of a 10-foot cube.

consts.name: dnpCarpenterWeeksPerCube
consts.comment: the 10-foot cube takes one week.

consts.name: dnpCarpenterCrewForDaily
consts.comment: seven characters (only one a carpenter) build the 10-foot cube in a day.

consts.name: dnpCarpenterPerWorkers
consts.comment: one carpenter is needed for every nine non-carpenter workers.

consts.name: dnpGemStonesPerDayDie
consts.comment: a gem cutter finishes rough gems at 1d10 stones per day.

consts.name: dnpPotterSmallMedPerDay
consts.comment: a potter creates two small or medium items per day.

consts.name: dnpPotterLargePerDay
consts.comment: or one large item per day.

consts.name: dnpPotterKilnDays
consts.comment: the pottery must then fire in the kiln an additional day.

consts.name: dnpPotterSmallCostCp
consts.comment: raw materials cost 3 cp for a small item.

consts.name: dnpPotterMediumCostCp
consts.comment: raw materials cost 5 cp for a medium item.

consts.name: dnpPotterLargeCostCp
consts.comment: raw materials cost 1 sp (10 cp) for a large item.

consts.name: dnpSmeltSmallMiners
consts.comment: a small smelter processes ore as fast as four miners produce it.

consts.name: dnpSmeltMediumMiners
consts.comment: a medium smelter processes the ore of up to 20 miners.

consts.name: dnpSmeltLargeMiners
consts.comment: a large smelter processes the ore of up to 100 miners.

consts.name: dnpSmeltSmallGpPerDay
consts.comment: a small smelting operation costs 5 gp per day to run.

consts.name: dnpSmeltMediumGpPerDay
consts.comment: a medium smelting operation costs 12 gp per day.

consts.name: dnpSmeltLargeGpPerDay
consts.comment: a large smelting operation costs 25 gp a day.

consts.name: dnpMasonWallThickFt
consts.comment: a stonemason builds a wall section one foot thick.

consts.name: dnpMasonWallLongFt
consts.comment: the wall section is 10 feet long.

consts.name: dnpMasonWallHighFt
consts.comment: the wall section is five feet high, in a day.

consts.name: dnpWeaveSqYardsPerDay
consts.comment: a weaver creates two square yards of material per day.

consts.name: dnpWeaponsmithFineDamageBonus
consts.comment: the fine-quality weapon inflicts +1 damage on all successful attacks.

consts.name: dnpWeaponsmithNat20AttackBonus
consts.comment: a natural 20 on the fine-quality check adds +1 to all attack rolls.

consts.name: dnpBlindAttackMod
consts.comment: blind-fighting suffers only -2 on attack and damage rolls and saving throws.

consts.name: dnpBlindStandardMod
consts.comment: the standard darkness penalty blind-fighting replaces is -4.

consts.name: dnpBlindDexReductionOnly
consts.comment: the Dexterity reduction for a blind-fighting character is only 1.

consts.name: dnpBlindClimbPenaltyOnly
consts.comment: the Climbing Rating penalty for a blind-fighting character is only -5 percent.

consts.name: dnpDirConcentrateRoundsDie
consts.comment: direction sense requires concentrating 1d6 rounds before the determination.

consts.name: dnpDirErrorDeg
consts.comment: a failed-but-greater-than-1 roll is off by up to 90 degrees left or right.

consts.name: dnpDirOppositeRoll
consts.comment: a Proficiency Check of 1 determines a direction exactly opposite the true one.

consts.name: dnpEnduranceTimeMult
consts.comment: endurance doubles the time a character can exert himself before fatigue and exhaustion.

consts.name: dnpFireDryMinutesDice
consts.comment: fire-building starts a fire in 2d20 minutes with dry wood and tinder.

consts.name: dnpFireAdverseMinutesDice
consts.comment: wet wood or high winds increase the time to 3d20 minutes.

consts.name: dnpFishChecksPerHour
consts.comment: fishing allows one Proficiency Check per hour spent fishing.

consts.name: dnpFishRationNum
consts.comment: one fish provides 1/2 the daily rations for one character (numerator).

consts.name: dnpFishRationDen
consts.comment: one fish provides 1/2 the daily rations for one character (denominator).

consts.name: dnpFungusDeadlyPct
consts.comment: approximately 50 percent of all fungi discovered underground are deadly poisonous.

consts.name: dnpFungusStudyTurns
consts.comment: the no-check study period is one turn.

consts.name: dnpHealEmergencyRounds
consts.comment: emergency healing must occur within one round of the wound being inflicted.

consts.name: dnpHealEmergencyDie
consts.comment: successful emergency healing recovers 1d3 hit points.

consts.name: dnpHealTravelHpPerDay
consts.comment: regular healing attention recovers 1 hit point per day without complete rest.

consts.name: dnpHealRestHpPerDay
consts.comment: under a healer a character at complete rest recovers 2 hit points per day.

consts.name: dnpHealPoisonSaveMod
consts.comment: immediate healing aid gives +2 to the saving throw vs. injected poison.

consts.name: dnpHealPoisonRestTurns
consts.comment: the aided character must remain at complete rest one turn.

consts.name: dnpHealPoisonAidRounds
consts.comment: the healer is completely occupied ministering for five melee rounds.

consts.name: dnpMountClimbBonusPctPerSlot
consts.comment: mountaineering grants +10 percent to the Climbing Rating per slot spent.

consts.name: dnpRideJumpFreeObstacleFt
consts.comment: no jump check is needed for obstacles three feet tall or less.

consts.name: dnpRideJumpFreeGapFt
consts.comment: no jump check is needed for gaps less than 12 feet wide.

consts.name: dnpRideJumpMaxObstacleFt
consts.comment: a successful check urges the mount to leap obstacles up to seven feet high.

consts.name: dnpRideJumpMaxGapFt
consts.comment: a successful check urges the mount across gaps up to thirty feet.

consts.name: dnpRideSpurFtPerRound
consts.comment: spurring adds six feet per round to the mount movement rate.

consts.name: dnpRideSpurMaxTurns
consts.comment: spurring lasts up to four turns.

consts.name: dnpRideSpurLeadTurns
consts.comment: after racing the steed must be walked by its dismounted rider for a turn.

consts.name: dnpRideShieldACBonus
consts.comment: hanging alongside the steed as a shield grants +6 to Armor Class.

consts.name: dnpRideDropMeleeFt
consts.comment: the mounted leap allows a melee attack on any creature within 10 feet.

consts.name: dnpRideDropMod
consts.comment: the mounted leap requires a Proficiency Check with a -4 modifier.

consts.name: dnpRideDropFailDie
consts.comment: a failed mounted leap falls clumsily and suffers 1d3 points damage.

consts.name: dnpRideKneesFailDie
consts.comment: failing the knees-guidance check after damage means falling: an additional 1d6 damage.

consts.name: dnpRopeLassoMod
consts.comment: rope use grants +2 on all attacks made with a lasso.

consts.name: dnpRopeClimbBonusPct
consts.comment: rope use grants +10 percent on all Climbing Checks made while using a rope.

consts.name: dnpRopeEscapeMod
consts.comment: escaping bound hands takes a Proficiency Check with a -6 penalty.

consts.name: dnpSlowAirPct
consts.comment: slow respiration drops air use to 10 percent of the resting rate.

consts.name: dnpSlowConcentrateTurns
consts.comment: the trance requires one turn of concentration in a restful position.

consts.name: dnpSoundMaxMiles
consts.comment: sound analysis calculates distances of up to one mile.

consts.name: dnpSoundLenPct
consts.comment: the successful-analysis margin of error for length: + or -30 percent.

consts.name: dnpSoundWidthPct
consts.comment: the margin of error for width: + or -25 percent.

consts.name: dnpSoundHeightPct
consts.comment: the margin of error for height: + or -25 percent.

consts.name: dnpSoundDetailRoll
consts.comment: a check of 5 or less also reveals additional details of the area.

consts.name: dnpXpPerGpNum
consts.comment: a business NPC gains 1 experience point (numerator).

consts.name: dnpXpPerGpDen
consts.comment: per 2 gp of income netted by his business (denominator).

consts.name: dnpXpNpcHpDie
consts.comment: such characters gain 1d4 hit points per level.

consts.name: dnpT10RowCount
consts.comment: The Table 10 census: 14 class rows.

consts.name: dnpT11RowCount
consts.comment: The Table 11 census: 14 craftsman rows.

consts.name: dnpT12RowCount
consts.comment: The Table 12 census: 11 weapon rows.

consts.name: dnpT13RowCount
consts.comment: The Table 13 census: 15 adventuring rows.

consts.name: dnpArrowheadsPerDayLo
consts.comment: the arrowhead rate: 1-2 arrowheads per day (low).

consts.name: dnpArrowheadsPerDayHi
consts.comment: the arrowhead rate: 1-2 arrowheads per day (high).

bools.name: dnpCheckLikeAbilityCheck
bools.comment: the Proficiency Check is made exactly like an Ability Check.

bools.name: dnpSuccessDegreeQuality
bools.comment: the exact amount of success determines the degree of workmanship.

bools.name: dnpNatural20Flawless
bools.comment: a 20 equals a nearly flawless creation.

bools.name: dnpMostUsesNoFailure
bools.comment: under normal conditions there is no chance of failure for most proficiency uses.

bools.name: dnpSlotsNeedNotBeFilled
bools.comment: characters are not required to fill all of their proficiency slots.

bools.name: dnpUnfilledSlotSaved
bools.comment: unfilled slots are saved and can be used at a later time.

bools.name: dnpFilledSlotCannotChange
bools.comment: once a slot is filled it cannot be changed for any reason.

bools.name: dnpWeaponSlotHoldsNonweapon
bools.comment: a weapon slot can be used for a nonweapon proficiency instead.

bools.name: dnpNonweaponSlotHoldsWeapon
bools.comment: the reverse is not allowed: a nonweapon slot cannot buy a weapon proficiency.

bools.name: dnpTimeAssumesFullDay
bools.comment: the listed proficiency time assumes the character devotes his entire working day.

bools.name: dnpDistractionIncreasesTime
bools.comment: time out to hunt, fight or yield to distractions increases the required time.

bools.name: dnpOptionalBonusesAllowed
bools.comment: the DM may modify and expand the nonweapon proficiency rules.

bools.name: dnpBackgroundAutoProficiency
bools.comment: the DM can rule a youth apprenticeship grants automatic proficiency in the skill.

bools.name: dnpTrainerDeclaresSpecies
bools.comment: the trainer must declare the creature type when the proficiency is first gained.

bools.name: dnpArmorFlawsArmorerDetects
bools.comment: only a character with armorer proficiency can detect the flaws, on careful inspection.

bools.name: dnpArmorPlateFittingsWeekly
bools.comment: field or full plate requires the wearer present at least once a week for exact fittings.

bools.name: dnpBlacksmithNeedsForge
bools.comment: blacksmithing requires a forge with a coal-fed fire and bellows, a hammer and an anvil.

bools.name: dnpBlacksmithNoSharpWeapons
bools.comment: a blacksmith cannot make armor or sharp weapons, only hammers, maces and iron objects.

bools.name: dnpBoatLargerNeedsShipwright
bools.comment: vessels larger than 60 feet require shipbuilding, outside underground exploration.

bools.name: dnpBowFailArrowFirstShot
bools.comment: a failed arrow breaks on the first shot.

bools.name: dnpBowFailBowBreaks
bools.comment: a failed bow has a limited lifespan and breaks on the unmodified 1.

bools.name: dnpBowFineFailWorthless
bools.comment: the fine-quality option: any failure means the weapon is worthless.

bools.name: dnpBowyerNeedsWeaponsmithHeads
bools.comment: a weaponsmith is required to fashion arrowheads; the bowyer does the rest.

bools.name: dnpGemCutterNoAssist
bools.comment: a gem cutter derives no benefit from nonproficient assistance.

bools.name: dnpGemCutterNeedsLightTools
bools.comment: the gem cutter needs a good light source, chisels, small hammers and hardened blades.

bools.name: dnpLeatherMakesArmor
bools.comment: the leatherworker makes leather armor, clothing, backpacks, saddlebags, saddles and harnesses.

bools.name: dnpMinerFindsAndSupervises
bools.comment: the miner proficiency is needed to find a mine site and supervise its operations.

bools.name: dnpSmeltCostsOnlyOperating
bools.comment: the smelter only costs money when operating.

bools.name: dnpSmeltStockpilePractice
bools.comment: ore is stockpiled and then smelted at maximum efficiency.

bools.name: dnpMasonOftenMortared
bools.comment: the stones are often but not always mortared together.

bools.name: dnpWeaverNeedsLoom
bools.comment: the weaver requires a spinning apparatus and a loom, working wool or cotton.

bools.name: dnpWeaponsmithFineFailWorthless
bools.comment: the weaponsmith fine-quality option: any failure means the weapon is worthless.

bools.name: dnpWeaponsmithEstimateByComparison
bools.comment: unlisted weapons are estimated by comparison to the listed ones.

bools.name: dnpAnimalNoiseMagicOnly
bools.comment: a successful check: only magical means distinguish the noise from the real animal.

bools.name: dnpAnimalNoiseFamiliarAuto
bools.comment: creatures very familiar with the real noise know a failed imitation automatically.

bools.name: dnpAnimalNoiseOthersWisdomCheck
bools.comment: other listeners get Wisdom Checks to detect the failed fake.

bools.name: dnpBlindNoACPenalty
bools.comment: blind-fighting characters suffer no penalties to Armor Class from darkness.

bools.name: dnpBlindRetainsSpecials
bools.comment: special abilities are retained: a thief can backstab and a ranger keeps giant-class damage in the dark.

bools.name: dnpBlindStumbleHalved
bools.comment: the chance of stumbling over a drop-off or falling from a sheer surface is halved.

bools.name: dnpBoatingMaxSpeed
bools.comment: a boating-proficient character insures the boat is propelled at maximum speed.

bools.name: dnpBoatingReducesCapsize
bools.comment: boating proficiency reduces the dangers of capsizing a canoe or kayak.

bools.name: dnpDirSecretDMRoll
bools.comment: the DM always makes the Proficiency Check for direction sense.

bools.name: dnpEnduranceNoFoodWaterExtension
bools.comment: endurance does not extend the time unaffected by lack of food or water.

bools.name: dnpFireNoTinderbox
bools.comment: the fire-builder does not normally need a tinderbox; flint and steel not required.

bools.name: dnpFireAdverseNeedsCheck
bools.comment: adverse conditions also require a successful Proficiency Check.

bools.name: dnpFishCountWisdomMinusRoll
bools.comment: the number of fish caught is the Wisdom score minus the d20 roll.

bools.name: dnpFungusStudyNoCheck
bools.comment: no check is needed with plentiful light and one turn of study.

bools.name: dnpHealInterruptResaves
bools.comment: if the patient is moved or the aid interfered with, an unmodified re-save vs. poison is required.

bools.name: dnpMountUsesSpikes
bools.comment: mountaineering allows climbing with the aid of spikes driven into rock.

bools.name: dnpRideVaultStillFree
bools.comment: vaulting into the saddle of a standing mount needs no check, even in armor.

bools.name: dnpRideVaultMovingCheck
bools.comment: vaulting a moving mount, or moving in the same segment, requires a check.

bools.name: dnpRideKneesCheckOnlyWhenDamaged
bools.comment: guiding with the knees needs a check only if the character takes damage while riding.

bools.name: dnpRideJumpBalkOnFail
bools.comment: a failed jump check means the mount balks and another check retains the seat or falls.

bools.name: dnpRideSpurCheckEachTurn
bools.comment: spurring requires a Proficiency Check each turn.

bools.name: dnpRideShieldNoArmorNoAttack
bools.comment: the steed-shield feat allows no attack and no armor; missed attacks strike the mount instead.

bools.name: dnpRopeClimbBonusIncludesBelay
bools.comment: the +10 percent includes attempts to belay companions.

bools.name: dnpSlowFullyAware
bools.comment: the trance character is fully aware of anything nearby and emerges at will.

bools.name: dnpSoundSilenceRequired
bools.comment: sound analysis requires conditions of absolute silence.

bools.name: dnpSoundStaccatoRequired
bools.comment: the sound must have a sharp staccato quality: a howl is ineffective, a click or loud hey works.

bools.name: dnpSoundFailLocksArea
bools.comment: a failed check means no further attempts by that character on the same area.

bools.name: dnpSoundAnnouncesParty
bools.comment: using sound analysis announces the presence of the party to listeners.

bools.name: dnpSoundCombinesAnimalNoise
bools.comment: sound analysis can be used in conjunction with the animal noise proficiency.

bools.name: dnpSwimRulesOnPageTwelve
bools.comment: the swimming proficiency is fully detailed under the swimming rules on page 12 (the R504 pins).

bools.name: dnpXpPcNeverEarns
bools.comment: player characters never earn experience points from proficiency use.

bools.name: dnpXpUseFighterTable
bools.comment: NPCs advanced this way use the level-advancement table for fighters.

bools.name: dnpXpDMMayAssignLevels
bools.comment: the DM may simply assign these characters additional levels without recording income.

bools.name: dnpHorsemanHasOneNonweapon
bools.comment: 0th-level horsemen and lancers have one nonweapon proficiency.

bools.name: dnpBardAsOtherClasses
bools.comment: the bard Table 10 row reads as other classes (the -1 sentinel).

tables.name: Table 10: CHARACTER PROFICIENCIES
col_comments: The initial weapon proficiencies by class row: cavalier 3, paladin 3, cleric 2, druid 2, fighter 4, barbarian 6, ranger 3, magic-user 1, illusionist 1, thief 2, acrobat 2, assassin 3, monk 1, bard as-other-classes (-1).
The initial nonweapon proficiencies: cavalier 2, paladin 2, cleric 3, druid 3, fighter 2, barbarian 3, ranger 2, magic-user 3, illusionist 3, thief 3, acrobat 3, assassin 2, monk 1, bard -1.
The weapon proficiency slots added per interval: 1 for every class.
The nonweapon slots added per interval: 1 for every class except magic-user and illusionist at 2.
The levels per added proficiency: cavalier 2, paladin 2, cleric 4, druid 5, fighter 3, barbarian 2, ranger 3, magic-user 6, illusionist 6, thief 4, acrobat 4, assassin 4, monk 2, bard 4.

tables.name: Table 11: CRAFTSMAN PROFICIENCIES
col_comments: The slots required: trainer 1, armorer 1, blacksmith 1, boatwright 1, bowyer/fletcher 1, carpenter 1, gem cutter 2, leatherworker 1, miner 2, potter 1, smelter 1, stonemason 1, weaponsmith 3, weaver 4 (the weaver and weaponsmith cells carry the grids-file image cautions).
The appropriate ability codes: 1 Wisdom, 2 Intelligence, 3 Dexterity, 4 Strength.

The die-roll modifier: armorer +2, blacksmith 0, boatwright -2, bowyer/fletcher -1, carpenter 0, gem cutter +2, leatherworker 0, miner -3, potter -2, smelter -2, stonemason -2, trainer 0, weaponsmith +3, weaver +4 (caution class as the slots column).
The asterisk flag: rows requiring a d20 roll for success each time used: animal trainer, bowyer/fletcher, miner, weaponsmith.

tables.name: Table 12: WEAPON MAKING
col_comments: The construction time in days: arrowhead is the -1 sentinel (1-2 per day, see the consts), battle axe 10, hand axe 5, dagger 5, heavy crossbow 20, light crossbow 15, fork/trident 20, spear/lance 4, shortsword 20, longsword 30, two-handed sword 45.

The material cost in copper pieces (the printed 10 sp = 100 cp, 2 gp = 200 cp): arrowhead 1, battle axe 100, hand axe 50, dagger 20, heavy crossbow 100, light crossbow 50, fork/trident 100, spear/lance 40, shortsword 50, longsword 100, two-handed sword 200.

tables.name: Table 13: ADVENTURING PROFICIENCIES
col_comments: The slots required: animal noise 1, blind-fighting 1, boating 1, direction sense 1, endurance 2, fire-building 1, fishing 1, fungus identification 1, healing 2, mountaineering 1, riding 1, rope use 1, slow respiration 1, sound analysis 1, swimming 1.
The appropriate ability codes: 1 Wisdom, 2 Intelligence, 3 Dexterity, 5 Strength, 0 NA - blind-fighting, endurance, mountaineering and slow respiration are NA.

The die-roll modifier, 99 = NA: animal noise -1, blind-fighting NA, boating +1, direction sense +1, endurance NA, fire-building -1, fishing -1, fungus identification +6, healing +2, mountaineering NA, riding +3, rope use 0, slow respiration NA, sound analysis -1, swimming 0.
The asterisk flag: direction sense, fishing and healing require a d20 roll each time used.
